extracted.intended_audience: DoD contracting officers, A-76 study teams, program managers, and source selection/evaluation personnel
extracted.subtask_short: conducting OMB A-76 competitive sourcing studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for planning, conducting, evaluating, and administering OMB A-76 competitive sourcing (commercial activity) studies within DoD, including PWS/QASP development, source selection, contract administration, and lessons-learned capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify what work is required, not how to do it
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid telling the bidders how they should accomplish the work, rather telling them what work is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If particular approaches to accomplishing a given task are necessary, then those requirements should be outlined in Section L of the solicitation. Additionally, such requirements should be outlined as evaluation criteria in the Source Selection Plan. ("avoid telling the bidders how they should accomplish the work, rather telling them what work is required." / "those requirements should be outlined in Section L ... as evaluation criteria in the Source Selection Plan.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add work requirements to 'get well' the commercial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The commercial activity should not assume it will gain additional manpower through the addition of work requirements not currently being done; adding work can leave the MEO without sufficient personnel if it wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessons learned cautioned against Government activities attempting to 'Get Well' as a result of the A-76 process; adding requirements not presently performed risks insufficient personnel and performance problems if the MEO wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates/skeleton PWSs only as tailored starting points
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixed reaction on use of skeleton or previously used PWSs: do not simply copy old PWSs; use them as a jumping off point and tailor requirements to specific needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates assist A-76 staff in developing the PWS and serve as a catalyst to completion within mandated timeframes, but avoid uncritical copying ("study group tends to copy the old PWS instead of formulating one to meet their specific needs").

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve contracting office personnel in PWS development
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel from the contracting office should be involved because they provide knowledge of contract requirements that must be represented in the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting personnel are critical in supporting the PWS team by providing knowledge of contract requirements that must be represented in the PWS. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Include database maintenance and government access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize database maintenance systems capable of updating the PWS when workload data changes and require government access to contractor-collected data on work performed and level of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requirements need to be included in the PWS and relevant contract clauses so workload changes during review and performance can be tracked and validated. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide contract type early and base it on Performance Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision as to the type of contract utilized should be based on the nature of work outlined in the Performance Summary; gain concurrence early and do not begin PWS/contracting documents until contract type is decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early concurrence prevents having to change documents later; work on PWS and contracting documents should not begin until the contract type is decided upon. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accurate workload data to avoid excess work/change orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate workload data is necessary to prevent work requirements from exceeding workload figures in the contract, which would require change orders and could drive up contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify workload figures carefully before award; inaccurate workload estimates create cost and administrative risk. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a robust Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: QASP is vital in both fixed-price and cost-reimbursement contracts to control costs and ensure contractor performance at specified levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP is a tool to discover discrepancies in the PWS that could raise contract price; an in-depth QASP is necessary to ensure contractor performs in accordance with contract terms and meets specified performance levels. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on functional expertise to choose surveillance methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality inspectors should not arbitrarily select a surveillance method (e.g., random sampling); rely on expertise of functional personnel responsible for implementing the surveillance plan to make method decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional personnel should guide surveillance methodology decisions to ensure technically sound monitoring. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Section L must instruct offerors what to provide and standardize formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Section L should include information as to what offerors should provide as part of their bid and standardize technical proposal formats to facilitate evaluation by the SSEB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific areas include what bidders should include in their technical proposal; requiring standardized formats facilitates SSEB evaluation and comparability. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Require staffing charts tied to cost proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors should be required to submit staffing charts showing proposed staffing levels and personnel positions that meet each PWS function, and manning levels should be equated to proposed hours in the Cost Proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking staffing charts to cost hours improves realism checks and evaluation clarity. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Require Past Performance Summary Matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors should provide a Past Performance Summary Matrix including vital information from similar contracts, technical points of contact, and data relating to past contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A uniform matrix facilitates assessment of past performance; include details that support evaluators in assessing relevance and quality. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB) early and avoid tainting
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the SSEB must be identified early to prevent them from becoming 'tainted' by participation in the Management Study or Independent Government Cost Estimate, and develop a list of personnel forbidden due to conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early identification and exclusion lists reduce conflict-of-interest risk and preserve evaluation integrity. (Refs. 21, 22)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish source selection criteria and include price realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands should formulate and publish source selection criteria to guide the decision process and include language in Section M indicating price realism will be a criterion in addition to lowest price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published criteria provide transparency and a clear evaluation basis for award decisions. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Require and evaluate a contractor phase-in plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase-in should be staggered over several months, a final date set for contractor assumption of responsibility and GFP, and the phase-in plan should be a solicitation requirement subject to evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staggered changeover reduces transition risk; include phase-in requirements in solicitation and evaluate proposals' plans. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a Contract Administration Plan (CAP) tied to the QASP
rubrics_metrics.description: A CAP should be developed for contract administration, including requirements to inspect in accordance with the QASP to ensure contractor compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In drafting the CAP, contracting officers should take advantage of functional personnel knowledge to ensure the plan is technically sound. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce Acceptable Quality Levels (AQL) and avoid extra-contractual inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the contractor is meeting AQLs and that inspectors do not levy requirements or inspections beyond the scope of the contract; contracting officers must correct improper inspections to avoid liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to correct improper inspector actions can obligate the Government to reimburse contractors for additional expenses (example of Board of Contract Appeals ruling). (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Address differences in existing site conditions cooperatively
rubrics_metrics.description: When site conditions differ from those stated in the contract, the Government should exercise care to avoid material breach; both parties should reach a mutually agreeable position to start the contract properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle condition differences early and cooperatively to preserve good relations and avoid breach claims. (Ref. 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and disseminate lessons learned in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Government employees and contractors supporting A-76 studies should be responsible for capturing lessons learned in writing and making them available to other commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO and others emphasized value of a comprehensive lessons learned system for A-76; disseminate best practices DoD-wide. (Refs. 20, 23)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct cost comparisons according to announced 'ground rules'
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency decisions to perform services in-house vs. contracting are reviewed to ascertain whether the agency followed the announced 'ground rules' for the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the A-76 team, especially contracting officers, conduct cost comparisons in accordance with criteria established within the solicitation; Comptroller General enforces adherence. (Ref. 24)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient solicitation information for intelligent competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Procuring agencies must provide prospective bidders with information sufficient to enable bidders to compete intelligently and on a relatively equal basis, though IFBs need not eliminate all uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguities can force bidders to take undue risk; agencies should clarify significant ambiguities but bidders are expected to account for inherent contract risk. (Ref. 25)

rubrics_metrics.name: Define technical evaluation areas and consequences for unacceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical compliance may be evaluated in specific areas—technical plan, organization and management plan, quality control, past performance, and transition plan—and any factor or sub-factor judged unacceptable will render the entire area unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make evaluation areas and pass/fail thresholds clear in the solicitation; failing one factor can make the offer technically unacceptable (WPAFB example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and mitigate organizational conflicts of interest early
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers should identify and evaluate potential organizational conflicts of interest early and avoid, neutralize, or mitigate significant potential conflicts before contract award (FAR 9.504).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts among evaluators (e.g., evaluators holding positions under study) can invalidate evaluations and lead to protest sustainment; staffing must comply with FAR guidance. (Ref. FAR 9.504)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear cost-accounting and cost-capture methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 circular provides guidance for cost comparisons but not the method commands are expected to use for capturing and recording costs; commands need a uniform, functioning cost-accounting method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of standard approach for non-standard costs (volunteers, prison labor), direct/indirect/G&A costs makes studies lengthy and difficult; establish clear cost-capture methods prior to study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider past performance and best-value aspects in evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76's cost-comparison emphasis can force decisions based solely on cost; past performance and best-value tradeoffs are important but A-76 provides limited guidance on measuring or incorporating them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents recommended inclusion and measurement of past performance in competition; consider modifying evaluation to better account for value beyond price rather than relying exclusively on lowest bid vs MEO bid process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish strong program management and governance for studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive sourcing studies require sound management structure—senior management involvement, adherence to timelines, resolution of stakeholder conflicts, and a sound acquisition strategy to manage risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider forming an 'A-76 Council' or Integrated Product Team (IPT), assign a full-time program manager, or use a 'quasi' program office approach similar to major weapon systems to handle study complexity and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff A-76 teams to meet schedules while preserving technical competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Installations should consider assigning full-time A-76 staff (including a full-time program manager) to meet timelines, but balance with risk that staff lose touch with the jobs under study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-time members focused on the study improve schedule compliance; to mitigate loss of technical competence, have team members work closely with the activities under study and leverage functional expertise. (Refs. 19)
